provenance.canonical-source: packages/core/src/dialog/{Dialog.tsx,Dialog.css,DialogHeader.tsx,DialogHeader.css,DialogContent.tsx,DialogContent.css,DialogActions.tsx,DialogActions.css,DialogCloseButton.tsx,DialogCloseButton.css,DialogContext.ts} plus packages/core/src/scrim/{Scrim.tsx,Scrim.css} for the backdrop and packages/core/src/utils/{useFloatingUI/useFloatingUI.tsx,usePreventScroll.ts} for the focus/scroll chassis. site/docs/components/dialog/accessibility.mdx read for the documented keyboard/focus contract; site/src/examples/dialog/{Default,CloseButton,Sizes,Preheader,WithoutAccent,Error}.tsx read for defaults. packages/core/src/drawer/{Drawer.tsx,Drawer.css} read only to fix the scope boundary.
provenance.accent-pin: sentiment-accent-background -> palette-accent, which carries a data-accent axis (blue default, teal alternate; next/palette/accent.css). This column pins BLUE, matching button/input/select.salt.json; only calendar.salt.json models byAccent. Recorded, not modelled.
provenance.surface: Dialog.css background: var(--salt-container-primary-background) -> next/characteristics/container.css -> palette-background-primary -> snow rgb(255,255,255) light / jet rgb(16,24,32) dark. DialogContent.css re-declares the SAME token on the body wrapper, which is reproduced by style.content.box rather than dropped.
provenance.fg: DialogContent.css color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground) -> next/characteristics/content.css -> palette-foreground-primary -> black/white. Also the preheader's colour via <Text color="primary"> -> .saltText-primary.
provenance.fg-secondary: DialogHeader.tsx renders the description as <Text color="secondary"> -> Text.css .saltText-secondary { --text-color: var(--salt-content-secondary-foreground) } -> palette-foreground-secondary -> gray-700 rgb(76,81,87) light / gray-300 rgb(177,181,185) dark.
provenance.divider: Dialog.css border-color and DialogContent.css scroll-divider colours are both var(--salt-separable-tertiary-borderColor) -> next/characteristics/separable.css -> palette-alpha-contrast-mediumLow -> next/palette/alpha.css: black-20a light / white-20a dark -> foundations/alpha.css rgba(<black|white>-rgb, 0.2). ONE token, three consumers (panel border, content top divider, content bottom divider).
provenance.scrim-bg: Scrim.css background: var(--saltScrim-background, var(--salt-overlayable-background)) -> next/characteristics/overlayable.css --salt-overlayable-background: var(--salt-palette-alpha-higher) -> next/palette/alpha.css: [data-mode=light] alpha-higher = color-white-65a, [data-mode=dark] alpha-higher = color-black-65a -> foundations/alpha.css rgba(255,255,255,0.65) / rgba(0,0,0,0.65). SALT'S LIGHT-MODE SCRIM IS WHITE. Grepped twice because it contradicts the usual expectation.
provenance.shadow-modal: Dialog.css box-shadow: var(--salt-overlayable-shadow-modal) -> overlayable.css -> --salt-shadow-medium -> next/palette/shadow.css: 0 12px 40px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.3) light / rgba(0,0,0,0.65) dark. The heaviest stop in Salt's five-stop scale (docs/foundations/elevation.md).
provenance.accent: DialogHeader.css .saltDialogHeader-withAccent::before background: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background) -> next/characteristics/sentiment.css -> palette-accent -> blue-500 rgb(0,120,207), identical in both mode blocks.
provenance.status-*: Dialog.css .saltDialog-{info,error,warning,success} { border-color: var(--salt-status-{s}-borderColor) } -> next/characteristics/status.css -> palette-{info,negative,warning,positive} -> the 500 stops, mode-invariant. Values reused verbatim from tooltip.salt.json / alert.salt.json / input.salt.json rather than re-derived. NOTE the enum is FOUR wide here (ValidationStatus, not FormFieldValidationStatus) because DialogProps.status is typed `ValidationStatus` and includes `info` — the same source file (status-indicator/ValidationStatus.ts) Salt's Input deliberately narrows with Omit<ValidationStatuses,"info">.
provenance.status-active: ONE indirection, two consumers, mirroring Tooltip.css's --tooltip-status-borderColor: the panel's border-color and the header StatusIndicator's colour both read it, so a single reassignment per status recolours both. Its default is var(--divider), i.e. the neutral separable-tertiary edge Dialog.css ships when no status is set.
provenance.byDensity.panel-padding: Dialog.css padding-top/padding-bottom: var(--salt-spacing-300); there is NO horizontal padding on .saltDialog. spacing-300 = 3 x spacing-100 = 12/24/36/48px (foundations/spacing.css; docs/foundations/spacing.md).
provenance.byDensity.panel-shape: Dialog.css border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner, 0) — the UNSUFFIXED corner stop, next/palette/corner.css [data-corner="rounded"] -> curve-150 -> foundations/curve.css 3/6/9/12px. A rounder stop than the corner-weak (curve-100, 2/4/6/8) that input/dropdown use.
provenance.byDensity.header-padding: DialogHeader.css padding-bottom/left/right: var(--salt-spacing-300); no padding-top declared.
provenance.byDensity.header-gap: DialogHeader.css gap: var(--salt-spacing-100) — the flex ROW gap between the status glyph / accent column and the text container. 4/8/12/16px.
provenance.byDensity.header-text-offset: DialogHeader.css .saltDialogHeader-container padding-top: calc((var(--salt-size-base) - var(--salt-text-h2-lineHeight)) / 2). size-base 20/28/36/44 (foundations/size.css) minus text-h2-lineHeight 18/24/32/42 (next/characteristics/text.css density blocks) over 2 = 1/2/2/1px. Computed per density, not assumed constant.
provenance.byDensity.accent-bar-width: DialogHeader.css .saltDialogHeader-withAccent::before width: var(--salt-size-bar) -> foundations/size.css 2/4/6/8px. FROZEN-TOKEN CHECK: size-bar is on the density scale, not the fixed scale, so this genuinely moves.
provenance.byDensity.accent-bar-bottom: same rule, bottom: var(--salt-spacing-300) = 12/24/36/48px — the bar stops above the header's own bottom padding.
provenance.byDensity.icon-size: DialogHeader.css `.saltDialogHeader .saltStatusIndicator.saltIcon { --icon-size: var(--salt-text-h2-lineHeight) }` -> 18/24/32/42px. NOT --salt-size-icon: Salt deliberately sizes this glyph to one line of the title beside it, which is why the frozen-token check finds nothing to unfreeze here.
provenance.byDensity.type-title: Text.css `h2.saltText { font-family: var(--salt-text-h2-fontFamily); font-size: var(--salt-text-h2-fontSize); font-weight: var(--salt-text-h2-fontWeight); line-height: var(--salt-text-h2-lineHeight) }`. FAMILY: next/characteristics/text.css keys the h2 family off [data-heading-font], and SaltProvider.tsx line 42 sets DEFAULT_HEADING_FONT = "Open Sans", so the default block (Open Sans + fontWeight-semiBold 600) applies, NOT the Amplitude block. SIZE/LINE-HEIGHT per density block: 14/18 - 18/24 - 24/32 - 32/42.
provenance.byDensity.type-body: the ambient .saltText body ramp (font-family openSans, font-size --salt-text-fontSize, line-height --salt-text-lineHeight, font-weight --salt-text-fontWeight = regular 400): 11/14 - 12/16 - 14/18 - 16/20. Used by BOTH the description and the preheader — the preheader is a plain .saltText nested inside the H2, and Text.css's heading rule is `h2.saltText, .saltText-h2.saltText`, which a nested span does not match.
provenance.byDensity.content-margin / content-paddi: DialogContent.css margin-left: var(--salt-spacing-200) (8/16/24/32), margin-right: var(--salt-spacing-300) (12/24/36/48), padding-left: var(--salt-spacing-100) (4/8/12/16). The asymmetry is in source and is intentional: margin-left + padding-left = spacing-300, so the text still aligns with the header, while the padding sits INSIDE the scroll container so a focus ring is not clipped.
provenance.byDensity.content-overflow-padding: DialogContent.css .saltDialogContent-overflow { padding-right: var(--salt-spacing-100) }, applied only while isOverflowing is true.
provenance.byDensity.actions-padding: DialogActions.css padding: var(--salt-spacing-300); padding-bottom: 0 -> `24px 24px 0` at medium.
provenance.size-breakpoint-pin: Dialog.tsx composes withBaseName(size, currentBreakpoint), producing fifteen classes. Salt computes the breakpoint in JS (utils/useResponsiveProp.ts useCurrentBreakpoint over breakpoints/Breakpoints.tsx DEFAULT_BREAKPOINTS xs:0 sm:600 md:960 lg:1280 xl:1920), so these are real classes, not media queries — but this generator has no @media channel and the template has one row per size, so ONE breakpoint column is carried. Pinned to `lg` (1280-1919px), the harness's own viewport, matching INPUT-MATRIX.md finding 9's desktop-value precedent. THE FULL MATRIX, from Dialog.css, width / max-height: small xs 100%/48%, sm 56%/48%, md 36%/48%, lg 24%/48%, xl 24%/48%; medium xs 100%/72%, sm 84%/72%, md 68%/72%, lg 48%/72%, xl 48%/72%; large xs 100%/84%, sm 96%/84%, md 84%/84%, lg 72%/84%, xl 72%/84%. Source carries the comment `/* Pending design decision on heights and widths */` above the block, recorded rather than smoothed over.
provenance.animation: Dialog.css .saltDialog-enterAnimation { animation: var(--salt-animation-fade-in-center) } and .saltDialog-exitAnimation { animation: var(--salt-animation-fade-out-back) } -> foundations/animation.css: `fade-in-center var(--salt-animation-duration) var(--salt-animation-timing-function)` and `fade-out-back var(--salt-animation-duration) ease-in-out both`, where --salt-animation-duration = --salt-duration-perceptible = 300ms and --salt-animation-timing-function = ease-in-out. BOTH keyframes are OPACITY ONLY — fade-out-back's name promises a transform its body does not contain (foundations/animation.css lines 149-156). Rendered here as the registry-neutral dialog-fade-in / dialog-fade-out keyframes appended to page/chrome.css.
provenance.no-scrim-animation: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: Scrim.css contains no animation, transition or keyframe reference. Salt's backdrop appears instantly beneath a panel that fades in — the same total-absence finding TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md recorded for Tooltip.css.
provenance.no-aria-describedby: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: `grep -rn aria-describedby packages/core/src/dialog` returns nothing. Salt wires aria-labelledby (via DialogContext) but never associates the description with the dialog.
provenance.no-panel-color: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: .saltDialog declares no `color`. The header inherits currentColor (Text.css's --text-color default) and only DialogContent declares content-primary-foreground, which is why style.panel.color is off here and style.content.color is on.
provenance.close-button-composition: DialogCloseButton.tsx renders <Button aria-label="Close dialog" appearance="transparent"><CloseIcon/></Button>; DialogCloseButton.css contains exactly three declarations (position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0). Every other visual property — size, corner, hover/focus/active states, icon dimensions — belongs to the composed Button and semantic-icon-provider. DECLARED COMPOSITION; only the placement is modelled.

structure.scrim.source: Dialog.tsx ConditionalScrimWrapper renders <Scrim fixed> around the floating component when showComponent && !disableScrim

structure.header-decoration.source: DialogHeader.css .saltDialogHeader-withAccent::before, applied when !disableAccent && !status; when a status IS set the bar is dropped and a <StatusIndicator status={status}/> renders in its place (DialogHeader.tsx)

structure.close-button.source: DialogCloseButton is a separate export the consumer adds; site/src/examples/dialog/Default.tsx has none, CloseButton.tsx adds one

structure.content-scroller.source: DialogContent.tsx renders .saltDialogContent wrapping .saltDialogContent-inner (overflow-y: auto), with a ResizeObserver overflow check and an onScrollCapture handler

behavior.aria-modal.source: Dialog.tsx line 154: aria-modal="true" on the FloatingComponent

behavior.background-suppression.source: Dialog.tsx focusManagerProps={{ context, initialFocus, outsideElementsInert: true }} — floating-ui's FloatingFocusManager applies the platform `inert` attribute to everything outside the dialog

behavior.focus-trap.source: FloatingFocusManager via useFloatingUI's DefaultFloatingComponent; documented in site/docs/components/dialog/accessibility.mdx (Tab wraps from last to first)

behavior.initial-focus.source: DialogProps.initialFocus?: ComponentProps<typeof FloatingFocusManager>["initialFocus"] — a tabbable index or a ref, default 0

behavior.focus-return.source: FloatingFocusManager returnFocus default; accessibility.mdx: 'When the dialog is closed, focus will return to the element that triggered the dialog'

behavior.dismiss-escape.source: Dialog.tsx useDismiss(context, { outsidePress: !disableDismiss }) — escapeKey is floating-ui's default and is never disabled here; accessibility.mdx documents Escape explicitly

behavior.dismiss-outside.source: Dialog.tsx useDismiss(context, { outsidePress: !disableDismiss }); disableDismiss defaults to undefined, so outsidePress is true

behavior.scroll-lock.source: Dialog.tsx passes lockScroll to FloatingComponent -> useFloatingUI.tsx usePreventScroll({ isDisabled: !lockScroll || !open }) -> usePreventScroll.ts preventScrollStandard(): documentElement.style.overflow = 'hidden' plus paddingRight = window.innerWidth - documentElement.clientWidth

behavior.described-by.source: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no aria-describedby anywhere in packages/core/src/dialog. Salt's description is visible text with no programmatic association.

behavior.exit-animation.source: Dialog.tsx useEffect keeps showComponent true for `300); // var(--salt-duration-perceptible)` after open flips false, and onAnimationEnd unmounts early if the animation finishes first

behavior.scroll-region-focusable.source: DialogContent.tsx overflowProps = isOverflowing ? { role: "region", tabIndex: 0, "aria-labelledby": headerId ?? dialogId } : {}

prop.size.source: DialogProps.size?: "small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium". Listed DEFAULT FIRST, per the convention select.shadcn.json set with ["default", "sm"] — the skeleton and the harness both take value[0] as the resting state, so a size-ordered list would have made every Salt dialog render small by default against source.

prop.status.note: no default — status is undefined unless set, so this list is in SOURCE order (status-indicator/ValidationStatus.ts ValidationStatusValues) rather than default-first
prop.status.source: DialogProps.status?: ValidationStatus -> status-indicator/ValidationStatus.ts ValidationStatusValues = [error, warning, success, info]. FOUR values, unlike Salt's own Input/Dropdown which take Omit<ValidationStatuses,"info">.

prop.disable-dismiss.source: DialogProps.disableDismiss?: boolean — 'Prevent the dialog closing on click away'. Escape is unaffected.

prop.disable-accent.source: DialogHeaderProps.disableAccent?: boolean; the withAccent class needs !disableAccent && !status, so a status also removes the bar

prop.show-close-button.note: no such prop — Salt's close button is an opt-in component, not a flag on the dialog

state.close-button-interaction.note: DialogCloseButton.css declares only position/top/right; every interaction state belongs to the composed Button (DECLARED COMPOSITION)

style.scrim.z-index.source: Scrim.css z-index: calc(var(--salt-zIndex-drawer) - 1) -> foundations/zindex.css zIndex-drawer 1200, so 1199 — deliberately one below the drawer layer and 101 below the modal layer the panel uses

style.scrim.animation.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Scrim.css has no animation or transition rule at all

style.panel.color.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — .saltDialog declares no color; DialogContent does (style.content.color) and the header inherits currentColor

style.panel.border.source: Dialog.css border: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) var(--salt-separable-tertiary-borderColor). size-fixed-100 is 1px on the FIXED scale, density-invariant by design (docs/foundations/sizes.md), so the literal is correct at every density. The colour goes through the --status-active indirection so the status rows recolour it.

style.panel.gap.note: Salt spaces its parts with per-part padding, not a container gap; adding one would double every seam

style.panel.width.note: width IS the size axis here — see style.panel.size@small/@medium/@large

style.panel.max-width.note: no absolute cap — the size classes set a percentage width

style.panel.max-height.note: set per size, not globally — see the size rows

style.panel.overflow.source: Dialog.css overflow-y: auto on .saltDialog itself, IN ADDITION to the inner content scroller — two nested scroll containers

style.panel.outline.note: no outline declaration; the platform default applies

style.panel.animation.source: Dialog.css .saltDialog-enterAnimation { animation: var(--salt-animation-fade-in-center) } -> fade-in-center 300ms ease-in-out; the keyframe body is opacity 0 -> 1 only

style.panel.animation@exit.source: Dialog.css .saltDialog-exitAnimation { animation: var(--salt-animation-fade-out-back) } -> fade-out-back 300ms ease-in-out both. Despite the name, foundations/animation.css's fade-out-back keyframe is opacity 1 -> 0 with NO transform.

style.accent-bar.box.source: DialogHeader.css .saltDialogHeader-withAccent::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; bottom: var(--salt-spacing-300); width: var(--salt-size-bar); background: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background) } — position/top/left live in the template's base, the three theme values here

style.header-icon.size.source: DialogHeader.css --icon-size: var(--salt-text-h2-lineHeight) on the composed StatusIndicator

style.header-icon.color.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION: the glyph itself belongs to StatusIndicator/semantic-icon-provider. Only the colour source is modelled, and it rides the SAME indirection the panel border reads, so one status reassignment moves both.

style.header-icon.offset.source: DialogHeader.css repeats calc((var(--salt-size-base) - var(--salt-text-h2-lineHeight)) / 2) on the StatusIndicator, the identical expression the text container uses

style.title.color.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — <H2> is given no color prop, so Text.css's --text-color default (currentColor) applies and the title inherits

style.preheader.font.source: the preheader is a plain .saltText nested inside the H2; Text.css's heading rule is `h2.saltText, .saltText-h2.saltText`, which a nested span does not match, so the body ramp wins

style.content.box.source: DialogContent.css margin-left: spacing-200; margin-right: spacing-300; padding-left: spacing-100; background: var(--salt-container-primary-background) — the background is re-declared on the body wrapper in source and is reproduced rather than dropped

style.content.scroll-divider.source: DialogContent.css .saltDialogContent-inner border-top/border-bottom: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) transparent. size-fixed-100 = 1px, density-invariant. The transparent reserve is the point: the box does not jump when a divider appears.

style.close-button.shape.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION — the corner belongs to the composed Button

style.close-button.glyph-size.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION — the glyph box belongs to the composed Button + semantic-icon-provider CloseIcon

style.close-button.opacity.note: no opacity rule; appearance="transparent" is a Button appearance, not a dimming

style.close-button.focus.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION — Button supplies its own focus ring
